A: Give the next steps as a numbered list with at least two steps (`1.`, `2.`).
Open with `Dear <full name>,` on the first line.
Never place a URL inside the body text. Links may appear only on a final line that starts with `Links:`.
Sign with the agent's name followed by a line that ends with `Support Team`.
Do not use contractions such as `don't`, `we'll` or `you're`.
B: Lead the main message with a sentence that starts with `Good news:` or `Quick update:`.
Invite a response with the exact phrase `reply to this email`.
Set expectations with a time frame written as `within <n> hours` or `within <n> business days`.
Point the customer to the relevant help-center article by including its `https://help.example.com/...` URL.
Open with `Hi <first name>!` on the first line.
Close with the agent's first name and then a line ending in `Support Team`.

relations.reason: The first line cannot open with `Dear <full name>,` and also with `Hi <first name>!`.
Both require the sign-off to be the agent's name followed by a line that ends with `Support Team`.
The help-center URL can be included while no URL appears in the body only if the URL is placed on a final line that starts with `Links:`, not inside a sentence as in the example of B.

reconciled: Point the customer to the relevant help-center article by including its `https://help.example.com/...` URL only on a final line that starts with `Links:` and comes after the signature, for example `Links: https://help.example.com/invoice-export`. Never place a URL inside the body text, and refer to the article there in words only.
